survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is an ICILS 2023 user guide/supplement describing questionnaire items, derived variables, and national adaptations; it does not provide an empirical analysis with an analytic sample. As such, it does not specify whether student sampling weights or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied in any model estimation. For secondary analyses using ICILS 2023 microdata, analysts should apply the complex survey design weights provided in the ICILS international database (IDB) and use the corresponding replicate weights when estimating standard errors, consistent with IEA’s standard scaling/estimation procedures. The supplements also document that some derived indices are based on IRT WLE scores (e.g., WLE with mean 50 and SD 10), but no weighting or replication strategy for model-based inference is described here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable because this document is a user guide and variable documentation rather than an empirical study predicting cognitive achievement outcomes with PV-based scores. It does not report any model estimation pipeline that would require specifying PV combination rules. Missing-data handling is not reported because no analytic dataset is constructed for hypothesis testing or prediction in this supplement; it only describes questionnaire content and how derived variables are computed from questionnaire responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined in this user guide/supplement. The document provides questionnaire items, derived-variable computation rules (e.g., recoding and IRT WLE scoring for indices), and lists of national adaptations by country. Therefore, no inclusion/exclusion criteria for an empirical student sample are applicable.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS 2023 supplement is a user guide describing questionnaire content (principal, ICT coordinator, teacher, and student questionnaires), national adaptations, and documentation of derived variables released in the ICILS 2023 international database. It does not present an empirical predictive or causal analysis, and it does not report model performance metrics, benchmarks, or effects. Instead, it specifies how certain indices are computed from questionnaire responses, including simple recoding and IRT-based WLE scoring for some scale indices (e.g., principal views on ICT outcomes and ChatGPT-related perceptions). Because no student-level achievement outcome is modeled and no PV-based scaling/combination is evaluated here, plausible values handling and missing-data handling for estimation are not part of this document’s scope. For secondary analyses, researchers should use the derived variables as documented and apply the ICILS IDB’s complex survey design weights and replicate procedures when conducting inferential modeling.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is intentionally sparse because the provided document is a technical user guide and variable documentation rather than an empirical research article. As a result, there is no reported analytic sample size, no country-by-country N table for an estimation dataset, no ML algorithm training/evaluation, and no reported outcome metrics. The document’s value is methodological: it defines questionnaire constructs and derived-variable computation (including IRT WLE scoring for some indices) and records national adaptations for comparability.
